ust.method: Overnight = New York closes strictly before each KOFIA close. Hedged = KTB 10Y minus β × US 10Y, β the trailing 26-week weekly beta known at the time. All variants walk-forward, z-scores vs trailing 52 weeks, thresholds ±0.5, hit rates over the next 4 weeks.

src: US Treasury daily par yields (2Y, 10Y; home.treasury.gov). Naver Finance: KOSPI and ETF weekly charts (KODEX 국고채30년액티브 439870, KODEX 200 069500). KOFIA: 10Y KTB final quote; freesis margin credit balance (신용공여 잔고) and investor deposits (투자자예탁금). Weekly, last trading day of each week.

method.window: 4-week changes; z-scores vs trailing 52 weeks (min 26); thresholds ±0.5
components: 30Y KTB ETF turnover share: 4-week avg minus 26-week avg

method.window: 20-day changes; z-scores vs trailing 260 sessions (min 130); bond ETF share 20-day avg minus 130-day avg; thresholds ±0.5; hit rates over the next 20 sessions; UST hedge β = trailing 130-day daily beta
components: 30Y KTB ETF turnover share: 20-day avg minus 130-day avg

notes.headline: KOSPI's rebound fails (−0.8%) and strong US payrolls nudge KTBs higher in yield: the 10Y +1.0bp to 3.863%, all of it the Treasury move. Over four weeks the KTB is −32bp, −14bp global and −18bp Korea's own rotation. Signal +1.41: bond rally
notes.now: KOSPI rose 2% intraday on Monday and then closed −0.8% at 5,018.85, its lowest close since Feb 2, as foreigners sold about KRW 0.7tn of stock, their seventh straight day and KRW 13.1tn in all, though they kept buying index futures. Margin credit is KRW 28.4tn (peak 38.5tn on Jun 19), down 12% in four weeks, and broker deposits 90.3tn, down KRW 9.8tn, so leverage is still being cut. The weekly signal is +1.41 (+2.07 on Friday; the daily version is +2.01): it eased only because the four-week window now starts after the mid-October slide, and KOSPI (−1.06, −11.5% in four weeks), margin (−1.60) and the KTB 10Y trend (−1.88) all still point to bonds, with the thin 30Y ETF part (+1.09) adding little. Over four weeks the US 10Y fell 24bp; at the weekly beta of 0.58 that explains −14bp of the KTB's −32bp, leaving −18bp of Korea-specific rally. Day to day, KTBs take about 0.46bp of every 1bp overnight Treasury move (R² 0.16 over the past year; 60-day beta 0.43, equal to its 1-year average, R² 0.25), more on Treasury rallies (0.55) than sell-offs (0.40), price it the same morning with almost no follow-through, and move the same way on 80% of big Treasury days. Monday's input was the US 10Y's 2bp rise after Friday's payrolls beat, which implied +0.9bp for the KTB against an actual +1.0bp, so the 10Y move was all global while the extra rise at the 1–3Y end was local hike pricing. The KTB 10Y yields 99.7bp less than the US 10Y, a new 1-year extreme. The signal's record is clearly better against Treasuries: hedged with β × US 10Y, rally calls were right 67% of the time and sell-off calls 69% (50% and 57% outright), with a Sharpe of 1.30 against 0.99 and a smaller worst drawdown (−26bp vs −36bp). Our read for the next 2–4 weeks: the rotation still favours KTBs over Treasuries, so we keep a beta-hedged long (KTB 10Y against about 0.6 × US 10Y) rather than add outright duration while a November 26 BOK hike is fully priced, 2s3s sits at a 1-year low and the KTB–UST gap is at its widest.
notes.flip: The signal needs KOSPI to recover about 10% over four weeks with margin credit rising again; Monday's failed rebound and continued foreign selling put a turn at least two to four weeks away, though the weekly reading will keep drifting lower as the October slide leaves the window. On the US side, watch the beta: if the 60-day beta (0.43 now) climbs back above 0.6, Treasuries dominate again and the hedge ratio should rise with it, and a hot US CPI (Nov 10) or weak 10Y/30Y auctions (Nov 10 and 12) would hit KTBs at about 0.4–0.46bp per bp; a November 26 BOK hike with hawkish guidance would turn the KTB-trend part against bonds even if stocks stay weak.
phases: KOSPI 2,400–2,900 and 10Y 3.1–4.2%. The signal was mostly neutral, and its few calls were driven by global yields rather than local rotation.
The BOK cut, the 10Y fell to about 2.7% and KOSPI drifted. Bond-rally readings around December 2024 worked.

KOSPI ran from about 2,800 to 7,500 by May 2026 on chip exports, and margin credit doubled to the high 30s (KRW tn). The signal read sell-off for most of the year while the 10Y rose from 2.8% to 3.9%. This was the signal's best stretch.
Peak, hikes and a false rally call
KOSPI peaked at 9,052 on Jun 19, then cracked. The signal called a bond rally, but the BOK hiked in July and August and the 10Y rose 35bp to a 4.54% high in September. Rotation lost to policy.

KOSPI fell 18% in October on AI-earnings and funding doubts and another 11% on Nov 5–6 (circuit breaker on Nov 6) as US blue-wave fears hit chips, and failed to rebound on Nov 9, with record foreign selling; the 10Y fell about 53bp to 3.86%. The signal has read bond rally since Oct 8 and has worked this time: the 10Y is 53bp below its level at the call.
notes.caveats: These are proxies, not reported fund flows. Margin credit and deposits come from KOFIA freesis daily statistics. The bond ETF share uses KODEX 국고채30년액티브 (439870), whose turnover is under 1% of KODEX 200's, so that part is weak. US Treasury levels are official par yields at the New York close, aligned to the last close before each KOFIA close, so the back-test never uses a US move the KTB market had not yet seen. The back-test starts in 2023 and covers one full equity cycle; most of the gain came after March 2025 (hedged Sharpe 1.97 vs 0.43 before), so treat the signal as a regime gauge alongside BOK pricing, not as a stand-alone trade. Adding the US 10Y trend as a fifth input made the signal worse (Sharpe 0.50 outright, 0.87 hedged), so Treasuries are used as the hedge and the attribution, not as a signal input.
